Crews power through another afternoon of ‘critical fire weather’ on East Evans Creek Fire

July 19, 2026

Fire officials report zero structures lost as of day 10 of 15,000-plus-acre fire; community meeting well attended

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 12:09
Instaread

Note: The Evans Creek Road Fire is burning approximately 26 miles north of Medford. The fire started Friday, July 10, at 2:41 p.m. after a car crashed into a power pole on East Evans Creek Road, sparking dry vegetation in the area about 7 miles west of Shady Cove, according to a post on the Jackson County Sheriff’s Office Facebook page. For ongoing updates, click here to go to the Rogue Valley Times story, or click here to go to the Jackson County evacuation map (zoom out to see the county as a whole). Check aqi.oregon.gov for current air quality readings (which are also posted on the Ashland.news homepage in the right-hand column above the weather).

By Buffy Pollock, Rogue Valley Times

Update 10:30 p.m.: Updated acreage for the East Evans Creek was reported at 15,015 acres, according to date posted to the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) just after 10 p.m. Sunday.

Update 9 p.m. The confirmed updated acreage of the East Evans Creek Fire was estimated at 14,442 acres according to data uploaded to the National Interagency Fire Center (NIFC) on Sunday night. With an increasing number of fires across the state — fire officials during a Sunday afternoon community meeting in Shady Cove — said an infrared flight for assessing fire size was not conducted on Saturday night. An infrared flight may or may not be conducted Sunday night.

A video of the Sunday community meeting is posted to the ODF Southwest Facebook page.

Update 8 p.m. Aggressive fire suppression efforts continued throughout Sunday despite another afternoon of critical fire weather. Strategic relocation of helicopters to an alternate base outside the morning inversion proved successful, allowing aircraft to begin flying earlier in the day and maximizing support for firefighters on the ground.

Structural tenders supported suppression efforts by supplying water to dip sites, helping helicopters maintain a steady pace of water-dropping operations throughout the day. Firefighters continues strengthening and connecting lines around the expanded Board Mountain spot fire area. Although crews were having success securing the perimeter, afternoon fire activity increased on the southern and eastern edges again pushing flames across fire control lines.

Firefighters remain actively engaged in the area southwest of Boswell Mountain with a large airtanker with retardant ordered to support suppression efforts. Structural resources remain positioned near homes in the Antioch, Jones Road and Pomeroy areas to provide structure protection while supporting wildland suppression operations.

On the Canyon Creek spot fire, firefighters quickly contained a roughly half-acre slop over after a burning tree fell across the control line, carrying embers into unburned vegetation west of the fire’s edge. Resources, including helicopters with water buckets, rapidly engaged the spot before it could spread further and are continuing mop-up operations. Structural resources remain assigned throughout the Shady Cove, Trail, Long Branch, and Dry Creek areas as part of a proactive structure protection plan.

Structural preparation has been completed in the Ramsey Canyon Road area, and crews are continuing to provide high-capacity pump support to increase water delivery for wildland operations. Tonight, across the main fire, firefighters will continue pushing mop-up farther into the fire footprint, increasing the depth of extinguished fuels behind established control lines.

Spotting potential remains elevated as exceptionally dry vegetation, heavy fuel loading, steep terrain, and persistent heat continue to support rapid fire spread. Critical fire weather remains the primary operational concern.

Update: 10:30 a.m.: JAC-127-A has been downgrades to Level 2-Be Set and JAC-127-A and JAC 127-B have been reverted to being one zone, JAC-127.

See previous coverage below

Firefighters on the 14,000-plus-acre East Evans Creek Fire worked overnight to hold and improve control lines, taking advantage of improved humidity recoveries to moderate fire behavior and secure areas impacted by heavy winds that kicked up Saturday night.

The fire was listed Sunday morning at 14,437 acres, up from 13,999 acres on Saturday, according to the WatchDuty app. Containment is at 8%.

According to a July 19 morning update, posted by Oregon Department of Forestry officials to Facebook on Sunday, crews continued engaging areas of the Board Mountain spot fire where fire crossed control lines on the southwestern edge south of Boswell Mountain. Firefighters made progress working to tie the spot fire into existing lines, though steep terrain and limited access continue to challenge suppression efforts.

Wildland and structural firefighting resources are being strategically repositioned early Sunday on the southern edge of the Board Mountain spot fire in order to take advantage of current conditions, strengthen suppression actions, and improve containment in that area before challenging conditions return this afternoon.

ODF officials on Sunday said, due to increased fire activity across the state, an infrared flight was not completed overnight. As a result, updated acreage and maps will not be available today.

The East Evans Creek Fire began just before 3 p.m. on July 10 — due to car crashing into a power pole and a downed line that sparked a grass fire — and grew from 2 acres to nearly 1,000 acres in just over three hours. The fire has grown exponentially each day since it began with resources pouring in from around the state and Governor Tina Kotek declaring a conflagration on July 13.

In addition to Oregon State Fire Marshal crews, a 10-member CAL FIRE crew was deployed Wednesday and joined the fire lines early Thursday under the Northwest Compact, a mutual aid agreement that enables western states to rapidly share firefighting personnel and resources during emergencies. On Thursday, Tualatin Valley Fire & Rescue from Washington County joined a strike team deploying to the fire with resources from Hillsboro Fire & Rescue and the Banks Fire District, along with firefighters from Gresham, the Port of Portland and Cannon Beach.

The main fire and the spot fire northwest of Hull Mountain remain in hold and mop-up status with crews strengthening existing lines, ODF officials said early Sunday, removing hazard trees and using handheld infrared technology to locate and extinguish remaining heat. On the Canyon Creek spot fire, firefighters maintained containment while continuing to deepen mop-up operations.

As structural crews continue detailed assessments of areas impacted by the fire and gain access to additional locations within the fire footprint, additional damage has been identified, including one primary residence that had been vacant for an extended period and five outbuilding structures with fire-related damage.

Structure protection efforts expanded into the Antioch, Pomeroy, and Jones Road areas amid worsening weather conditions with crews conducting structural preparation and improved water availability, building on earlier planning efforts to ensure a rapid and effective response as conditions evolve.

Aircraft will support ground operations as conditions allow. To improve early-day aviation access, five of the helicopters have been relocated out of the inversion zone, allowing the aircraft to begin flying earlier in the day as visibility improves.

A community meeting is planned at 2 p.m. today at Shady Cove School Gym, 100 Cleveland St., Shady Cove, to provide operational updates to community members impacted by the fire. The meeting can be streamed via ODF Southwest’s Facebook page, Facebook.com/ODFSouthwest, and will be available on replay.

Evacuations

There are evacuations in place in both Jackson and Douglas counties, issued by both counties’ Sheriff’s Offices and Emergency Management. Up-to-date evacuations are available here: https://readyjacksonco.com/Emergency/emergency-information-hub-east-evans-creek-road-fire
Find your evacuation zone here: https://tinyurl.com/EastEvansCreekFireEvacMap

Residents are urged to adhere to evacuation notices. A Level 3 evacuation notice means that danger to your area is current or imminent, with significant threat to life, and you must evacuate immediately. Updated evacuation notices, as of Sunday morning, included the following:

  • Level 3 – Go Now
  • JAC-109, JAC-017, JAC-124, JAC-126, JAC-149-B
  • Level 2 – Be Set
  • JAC-016, JAC-026, JAC-111, JAC-112, JAC-127, JAC-131, JAC-132, JAC-133, JAC-134, JAC-147, JAC-148, JAC-149-A, JAC-203-B
  • Level 1 – Be Ready
  • JAC-003, JAC-004, JAC-014, JAC-036, JAC-158, JAC-203-A, SHC-151, SHC-152, SHC-153, SHC-154, SHC-156, SHC-157; (Douglas County) DOU-1012, DOU-1015

Visit Genasys Protect at protect.genasys.com to find your zone and get updated evacuation levels.

Water concerns

On Thursday evening, Sunstone Water, which provides a portion of the city of Shady Cove with water, urged customers to conserve water supplies during ongoing efforts to battle the fire. Jackson County Fire District 4 officials said regional and state fire officials are aware of supply restrictions and working to ensure adequate supplies form other sources.

Road/Land Closures

The Tiller-Trail Highway is closed at the county border in Jackson County to Highway 62. Traffic is closed to the public on East Evans Creek Road at Meadows Road. The BLM has issued a road closure for West Fork Evans Creek Road and Rock Creek Road. Please avoid the fire area to allow firefighters and heavy equipment to operate safely. Road closure information is available on tripcheck.com.

A closure order for BLM-administered lands near the East Evans Creek Fire is in place. Public entry, including hunting, hiking, and camping, is prohibited. More information about the closure, including a map, is available on blm.gov/orwafire.

Numerous public and private trail areas within the Jackson Cooperative Travel Management Area (JACTMA) are currently closed due to wildfire conditions. Officials note that the largest component of closure within the JACTMA is the Olson Mountain Tract, which is accessed between Cobleigh Road and the Butte Falls-Prospect Highway, including the Medco A & B roads, and Vine Maple Mainline from the east (Near Medco Pond). For full information on closures, visit myodfw.com.

Smoke Impacts

Smoke from the East Evans Creek Fire may settle into valleys and other low-lying areas, reducing visibility and impacting air quality in nearby communities. Smoke conditions can change throughout the day as winds shift. Individuals sensitive to smoke should take appropriate precautions. For current air quality information and smoke forecasts, visit fire.airnow.gov.

Shelter

A Red Cross shelter is open for evacuees at Eagle Point Middle School, 477 Reese Creek Road. The previous shelter location at Hanby Middle School in Gold Hill is now closed. Pets are welcome at the shelter in Eagle Point but are not allowed inside the building. Red Cross officials will set up an area on the property to accommodate pets.

Horses can be taken to the Jackson County Expo at 21 Peninger Road, Central Point. Expo staff and volunteers are prepared to receive horses; however, call 541-776-7206 first to confirm space is available, as additional shelter locations may be activated. Owners should bring feed, water containers and any necessary medications when possible. For livestock sheltering assistance, call 541-776-7206.

RV parking

RV parking for those displaced by the East Evans Creek Fire is being made available at the Medford Gun Club (1259 E. Vilas Road, Central Point) and Trail Christian Fellowship (18881 Hwy. 62, Eagle Point).

Temporary Flight Restriction (TFR)

A “TFR” is in place for the fire area daily (24 hours) until further notice. Complete information is available online at tfr.faa.gov. Flying a drone near or around a wildfire is illegal and compromises the safety of both pilots and firefighters and interferes with firefighting efforts.

Reach reporter Buffy Pollock at 458-488-2029 or bpollock@rv-times.com. Follow her on Twitter @orwritergal. This story first appeared in the Rogue Valley Times. Email Ashland.news at news@ashland.news.
